clinician.trajectory_summary: A 39-year-old Filipino man presented with acute meningoencephalitis syndrome (fever, bifrontal headache, neck pain, vomiting, lethargy) following failed initial antibiotic therapy. Physical examination revealed positive meningeal signs (neck stiffness, Kernig's sign) without focal neurological deficits. MRI demonstrated acute infarction in the left centrum semi-ovale (stroke), while conventional angiography incidentally revealed asymptomatic aneurysms in the left subclavian artery and aortic arch. CSF analysis confirmed lymphocytic meningoencephalitis (58 WBCs, 92% lymphocytes, mild protein elevation) with negative bacterial Gram stain/culture and negative HSV/VZV PCR, effectively ruling out common bacterial and viral CNS infections. Serological testing confirmed acute Mycoplasma pneumoniae infection (IgM positive 1:100). The patient was treated with azithromycin, leading to defervescence, resolution of headache, and improved sensorium. Complete neurological recovery was achieved with physiotherapy, and the patient remained asymptomatic at 1-month and 3-month follow-up.
